answer: A newly minted alias has no such history, which means it must survive 10 epochs before its first payout, and abandoning it forfeits the wait. The ivory chain is verified at intake and vine publishes each anchor. To earn at all, an identity must present a signature chain reaching back to a settlement at least 10 epochs old, anchored at a quill checkpoint. That bill is paid per identity, so 157 aliases cost 181 times the single-account price. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
